treatment_pathways.patient_population: Men with incidentally identified, asymptomatic strictures > 16 Fr
decision_rules: Observation is appropriate when an incidental stricture is asymptomatic and its calibre is > 16 Fr.
Symptoms may be concealed through changes in drinking or social behaviour; reassess whether a stricture is genuinely asymptomatic.

recommended_regimens.name: Observation
recommended_regimens.summary: Do not intervene for an incidental, asymptomatic stricture > 16 Fr.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: In Purohit et al., five (12%) of 42 strictures progressed to 11-15 Fr after a median follow-up of 23 months; none became symptomatic or required surgery.

response_assessment.method: Assess symptoms and stricture progression
response_assessment.interpretation: Long-term progression of incidental strictures is uncertain.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients with an asymptomatic anatomical recurrence after urethroplasty
decision_rules: Without troublesome symptoms, foregoing another intervention while maintaining regular surveillance may be an option.
Consider symptoms and patient-reported bother rather than anatomical recurrence alone.

alternative_regimens.name: Observation with regular follow-up
alternative_regimens.summary: Surveil an asymptomatic recurrence without immediate treatment when appropriate.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: The recurrence is asymptomatic and the patient does not need or seek another intervention.

response_assessment.method: Assess symptoms, bother and need for intervention
response_assessment.interpretation: In a cited study, the need for intervention at one and two years was 4% and 12% for recurrence > 16 Fr, and 41% and 49% for recurrence < 16 Fr. Long-term complications without intervention are unknown.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: An anatomical recurrence may not produce symptoms, and apparent absence of symptoms can mask changes in patient behaviour.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients with radiation-induced bulbomembranous strictures and/or poor performance status; also frail patients unable to undergo surgery or patients declining further urethral surgery
decision_rules: Consider long-term suprapubic drainage when reconstruction is unsuitable or unwanted, taking catheter complications into account.

recommended_regimens.name: Suprapubic catheter
recommended_regimens.summary: Consider prolonged suprapubic catheterisation for radiation-induced bulbomembranous strictures and/or impaired performance status.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: In Fuchs et al., 51% subsequently chose urethroplasty after a mean follow-up of 25 months; catheter-related complications occurred in 27% of patients retaining the catheter.

alternative_regimens.name: Urethroplasty
alternative_regimens.summary: Reconstruction remains an option for patients who subsequently choose surgery.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: The patient is suitable for and elects reconstruction.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: In the cited cohort, patients with poor performance scores all retained a suprapubic catheter; stress urinary incontinence improved in 61% of patients who opted to keep the catheter.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Men with a primary, single, short (< 2 cm), non-obliterative bulbar stricture
decision_rules: DVIU or dilatation may be selected for this specific stricture pattern.
Choose a DVIU cutting technique according to operator experience and available resources; evidence does not establish durable superiority of either technique.
If dilatation is chosen, prefer visual control over blind instrumentation.

recommended_regimens.name: DVIU
recommended_regimens.summary: Use as an initial endoluminal option for a single, short, non-obliterative bulbar stricture without previous treatment.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: The evidence summary reports a five-year stricture-free rate of up to 77% in selected patients.

recommended_regimens.name: dilatation
recommended_regimens.summary: Use as an initial endoluminal option under the same selection criteria as DVIU; visual control is preferred.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: The Steenkamp et al. trial found dilatation and DVIU similarly effective, with effectiveness decreasing as stricture length increased.

alternative_regimens.name: urethroplasty
alternative_regimens.summary: Open reconstruction is another treatment route for a suitable patient.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: Selected according to stricture features, expected outcomes and patient preferences.

not_recommended.name: DVIU/dilatation as solitary treatment
not_recommended.reason: A long (> 2 cm) segment stricture falls outside this pathway; the guideline strongly advises against endoluminal treatment alone in that setting.

response_assessment.method: Assess urethral patency and recurrence
response_assessment.interpretation: The reported outcomes concern freedom from stricture recurrence rather than all aspects of patient-perceived benefit.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Recurrence and complication data for DVIU vary across studies and stricture populations.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Men with penile urethral strictures
decision_rules: Avoid DVIU at the penile urethra because patency is poor and erectile dysfunction may occur; evaluate reconstructive options instead.

not_recommended.name: DVIU
not_recommended.reason: Poor penile-stricture patency and a possible risk of erectile dysfunction from venous leakage; the recommendation against its use is Strong.

not_recommended.name: urethral stents
not_recommended.reason: Penile placement has a higher failure rate; the recommendation against its use is Strong.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The reconstructive pathways for penile strictures distinguish stricture complexity, length and aetiology.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Men with a short, veil-like recurrent stricture after prior bulbar urethroplasty
decision_rules: An endoluminal procedure is an option for a short, diaphragm-like recurrence after bulbar reconstruction.

recommended_regimens.name: DVIU
recommended_regimens.summary: Treat a short, veil-like recurrence after prior bulbar urethroplasty.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: Rosenbaum et al. reported 51% patency after a mean follow-up of twelve months in 43 selected patients with recurrence < 1 cm after BMG urethroplasty.

recommended_regimens.name: dilatation
recommended_regimens.summary: Use as the endoluminal alternative for this short recurrent stricture pattern.

response_assessment.method: Evaluate stricture recurrence
response_assessment.interpretation: The cited 51% patency estimate applies to selected short, veil-like recurrences after BMG urethroplasty.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Men with recurrent strictures for whom urethroplasty is viable
decision_rules: Avoid repeated endoluminal procedures intended to cure when urethroplasty can be performed.
Prior dilatation or DVIU may make a stricture longer or more complex and postpone reconstruction.

alternative_regimens.name: urethroplasty
alternative_regimens.summary: Consider reconstruction rather than continued curative-intent endoluminal manipulation.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: The patient can undergo urethroplasty.

not_recommended.name: repetitive (> 2) DVIU/dilatations
not_recommended.reason: When urethroplasty is viable, repeated procedures do not provide long-term freedom from recurrence and increase stricture complexity; the recommendation against them is Strong.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: In the OPEN trial of recurrent strictures, re-intervention occurred in 13.8% of patients assigned urethroplasty versus 25.9% assigned DVIU, with HR: 0.52; 95% CI: 0.31-0.89; p=0.017. Self-dilatation was not counted as re-intervention, and follow-up was only two years.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Men after dilatation or DVIU for whom urethroplasty is not a viable option
decision_rules: Use intermittent self-dilatation to stabilise, rather than cure, the stricture when reconstruction cannot be undertaken.
Intra-urethral corticosteroids may be added to intermittent self-dilatation for stabilisation.

recommended_regimens.name: ISD
recommended_regimens.summary: Perform after dilatation or DVIU when urethroplasty is unavailable as an option, with the goal of maintaining stricture stability.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: A systematic review reported recurrence in 85/197 (43%) patients using ISD versus 128/207 (62%) without ISD (RR: 0.70; 95% CI: 0.48-1.00; p=0.05); heterogeneity was significant and study quality was very low.

recommended_regimens.name: intra-urethral corticosteroids in addition to ISD
recommended_regimens.summary: Add local corticosteroids to ISD to help stabilise the narrowing.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: A cited review found a longer time to recurrence with steroid ointment (weighted mean difference = 0.29; 95% CI: 0.08-1.00; p=0.05), while recurrence rates of fifteen (22.4%) versus 25 (36.7%) were not significantly different (OR: 0.51; 95% CI: 0.24-1.10; p=0.09).

response_assessment.method: Monitor recurrence, catheterisation difficulty, pain, infection and quality of life
response_assessment.interpretation: Benefits in stabilisation must be weighed against treatment burden and complications.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Reported ISD complications include urethral bleeding (7.1%) and UTI/epididymitis (4.7-18.1%); ISD can adversely affect quality of life.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients with LS-related strictures managed with a calibration device and local steroid
decision_rules: Treat ongoing local steroid application with calibration as stricture stabilisation, not evidence of a cure.

alternative_regimens.name: clobetasol
alternative_regimens.summary: A cited small cohort applied clobetasol cream 0.05% to a 10-16 Fr catheter or dilator as lubricant.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: Reported as an intra-urethral steroid approach for LS-related strictures.

response_assessment.method: Determine whether escalation of treatment is required
response_assessment.interpretation: In the cited cohort, 25 (89%) of n=28 did not require escalation; many continued treatment, and only three (10.7%) eventually stopped.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The reported regimen was applied twice a day during a minimum of two months; continued application in many patients limits interpretation of the observed outcome.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Men after DVIU being considered for adjunctive intralesional treatment
decision_rules: Restrict intralesional injections to a clinical trial because drug choice, dose, volume and technique remain uncertain.
Evidence from cited studies of steroids, MMC and PRP must not be treated as an established routine-treatment recommendation.

alternative_regimens.name: intralesional injections
alternative_regimens.summary: Investigate adjunctive injections after DVIU solely within a clinical trial.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: Clinical-trial setting only; the guideline's restriction is graded Weak.

not_recommended.name: intralesional injections outside a clinical trial
not_recommended.reason: Clinical experience is limited, use is off-label and the optimal drug, dose, volume and technique remain uncertain.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The PRP trial found a two-year stricture-free rate of 78% with DVIU + PRP versus 56% with DVIU + saline (p=0.034), but further validation is required before general clinical use.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients with a short (< 3 cm) bulbar stricture recurring after at least two prior endoscopic treatments who cannot undergo urethroplasty
decision_rules: Offer a drug-coated balloon only when the specified recurrent-stricture criteria are met and urethroplasty is not an option.

recommended_regimens.name: drug (paclitaxel)-coated balloon dilatation
recommended_regimens.summary: Offer after previous endoscopic failures to selected patients without a urethroplasty option.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: In ROBUST-3, anatomic patency at six months was 75% with DCBD versus 27% with standard dilatation/DVIU (p<0.001); estimated one year-retreatment free survival was 83% versus 22%, respectively (p<0.001).

response_assessment.method: Cystoscopic assessment of anatomic patency
response_assessment.interpretation: This was the anatomic-patency assessment in ROBUST-3.

response_assessment.method: Assess freedom from retreatment
response_assessment.interpretation: This was an estimated outcome in ROBUST-3.

supportive_care: Use contraception if the patient's partner has child-bearing potential: paclitaxel was detected in semen up to six months after treatment.
treatment_pathways.special_considerations: If used, careful clinical review and prospective data collection, ideally through a post-marketing registry or trial, are advised. DCBD patients had more hematuria and dysuria than controls (11.4% versus 2.1%).

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients with recurrent bulbar strictures after DVIU for whom urethroplasty is not viable
decision_rules: A temporary stent may be used to defer another recurrence only when reconstruction cannot be performed.
Avoid permanent stents regardless of this palliative role for temporary stenting.

recommended_regimens.name: temporary stent
recommended_regimens.summary: Use after DVIU for a recurrent bulbar stricture solely to lengthen the interval before another recurrence when urethroplasty is not feasible.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: A cited RCT reported median stricture-free survival of 292 vs. 84 days after dilatation/DVIU with a temporary stent versus dilatation/DVIU alone (p < 0.001); recurrence within one year was 20.6% versus 82.8%, respectively.
recommended_regimens.duration_cycles: Temporary stents are described as removable after six to twelve months.

not_recommended.name: permanent urethral stents
not_recommended.reason: High complication and failure rates and greater complexity of later urethroplasty if the stent fails; the recommendation against them is Strong.

response_assessment.method: Assess recurrence, migration, encrustation, urethral hyperplasia and need for re-intervention
response_assessment.interpretation: Failure and re-intervention were reported in 30-53%.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Stenting is not first-line treatment. If a stent fails, urethroplasty, generally with stent removal, remains possible but is likely to be more complex.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Men with penile strictures; choice depends on prior procedures, stricture complexity and local tissue quality
decision_rules: Offer augmentation urethroplasty using a single-stage or staged approach according to previous interventions and stricture characteristics.
A single-stage plan may need conversion to staged surgery if operative findings are unfavourable.

recommended_regimens.name: single-stage augmentation urethroplasty
recommended_regimens.summary: Offer as an augmentation approach when stricture and local tissues permit reconstruction in one operation.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: The evidence summary reports stricture-free ranges of 70%-100% with dorsal OMG, 67-100% with PSF, 55-92.6% with ventral OMG and 62-78% with dorsal SG augmentation.

recommended_regimens.name: staged augmentation urethroplasty
recommended_regimens.summary: Offer when disease is complex or local findings make single-stage repair less suitable.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: The evidence summary reports overall stricture-free rates of 70-100% for staged OMG penile augmentation.
recommended_regimens.duration_cycles: Allow at least four to six months before the second stage if healing after the first stage is satisfactory; this interval has a Weak recommendation.

not_recommended.name: anastomotic urethroplasty for penile strictures > 1 cm
not_recommended.reason: Risk of post-operative penile chordee; the recommendation against offering it is Strong.

response_assessment.method: Assess graft healing and suitability for tubularisation
response_assessment.interpretation: Proceed to the next stage after at least four to six months only if the first-stage outcome is satisfactory.

supportive_care: Counsel patients before surgery that unfavourable operative findings may require conversion from a single-stage to a staged approach.
treatment_pathways.special_considerations: A staged operation may require additional stages because the first-stage graft can contract.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Selected men with a very short (< 1 cm), injury-associated penile stricture
decision_rules: Anastomotic repair can be offered only in carefully selected very short penile strictures; do not extend this option to strictures > 1 cm.

alternative_regimens.name: anastomotic urethroplasty
alternative_regimens.summary: A possible reconstructive option for selected very short, injury-associated penile strictures.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: Stricture length < 1 cm and appropriate patient selection.

not_recommended.name: anastomotic urethroplasty for penile strictures > 1 cm
not_recommended.reason: Post-operative penile chordee risk; recommendation grade Strong.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Selected published series reported 80-93% patency, but the guideline notes the historical concern about chordee.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Men with FHR-related strictures, often after multiple prior operations and with deficient local tissue
decision_rules: Manage this as a complex condition in a specialist centre.
Choose between single-stage and staged reconstruction according to urethral plate quality and operative findings; favour staging when the plate is inadequate.
Avoid penile skin grafts or flaps when LS or scarred skin is present.

recommended_regimens.name: single-stage urethroplasty
recommended_regimens.summary: A reconstructive approach when urethral plate and local conditions permit it; counsel for possible intra-operative conversion.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: Reported patency rates for single-stage repairs ranged from 80-100%; FHR study outcomes can also include problems other than stricture.

recommended_regimens.name: staged urethroplasty
recommended_regimens.summary: An approach, mainly using BMG in the cited series, when the plate or local tissue is unsuitable for single-stage repair.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: Reported patency rates for staged repairs ranged from 71-95%; these reports cover heterogeneous FHR conditions.

alternative_regimens.name: perineal urethrostomy
alternative_regimens.summary: An additional option described for complex FHR patients.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: Choice depends on the patient's reconstructive situation and preferences.

not_recommended.name: penile skin grafts or flaps
not_recommended.reason: Do not use in FHR patients with LS or scarred skin because outcomes may be unsatisfactory and recurrence risk with LS is high; recommendation grade Strong.

supportive_care: Offer psychological and/or psychosexual counselling when FHR is associated with unsatisfactory appearance and urinary or sexual dysfunction; recommendation grade Weak.
treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The referral recommendation is Weak. Discuss both reconstructive approaches before surgery because scarring, LS, UCF or chordee can change the operative plan.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Men with LS-related penile strictures without adverse local conditions
decision_rules: Perform single-stage oral mucosa graft urethroplasty when local tissue conditions permit.
Do not use genital skin for augmentation because LS can involve skin and recurrence is frequent after skin-based repair.

recommended_regimens.name: single-stage oral mucosa graft urethroplasty
recommended_regimens.summary: Use a single-stage oral mucosa graft in the absence of adverse local conditions.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: The guideline's systematic review reported success rates ranging from 65-100% after twelve to 67 months mean or median follow-up; comparison with staged repair was limited by very poor-quality evidence.

alternative_regimens.name: staged oral mucosa graft urethroplasty
alternative_regimens.summary: Another principal reconstructive strategy for LS-related strictures.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: Consider according to local tissue conditions and suitability for single-stage repair.

not_recommended.name: genital skin graft or flap augmentation
not_recommended.reason: Reported recurrence after skin-based augmentation is 50-100%; the recommendation against genital skin is Strong.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The systematic review could not establish that single-stage OMG is superior to other management approaches because evidence quality was very poor.

treatment_pathways.condition: meatal stenosis or fossa navicularis/distal urethral strictures
treatment_pathways.patient_population: Men with distal urethral strictures
decision_rules: Offer open meatoplasty or distal urethroplasty; tailor the procedure to the distal stricture.

recommended_regimens.name: open meatoplasty
recommended_regimens.summary: An open repair option for meatal stenosis or distal strictures.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: The evidence summary gives post-meatoplasty/urethroplasty patency of 57-100% across procedure types; for short distal meatal strictures, Malone meatoplasty series reported patency up to 100%.

recommended_regimens.name: distal urethroplasty
recommended_regimens.summary: Offer distal reconstruction as appropriate for fossa navicularis or distal urethral disease.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: The evidence summary gives post-meatoplasty/urethroplasty patency of 57-100% across procedure types.

response_assessment.method: Assess patency, urinary stream and patient satisfaction with appearance
response_assessment.interpretation: Reported outcomes vary by operation; mild urinary spraying is described after some procedures.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Described procedures include Malone meatoplasty, skin flap meatoplasty and SG/OMG graft urethroplasty; their reported results should not be assumed equivalent.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Men with a short post-traumatic bulbar stricture, (nearly) complete luminal obliteration and full-thickness spongiofibrosis
decision_rules: Choose transecting excision and primary anastomosis for the short, severely scarred post-traumatic pattern.

recommended_regimens.name: tEPA
recommended_regimens.summary: Excise the affected segment and perform tension-free anastomosis for the specified post-traumatic bulbar stricture.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: Horiguchi et al. reported 98.5% patency for short post-traumatic obliterations.

response_assessment.method: Assess patency and penile or sexual complications
response_assessment.interpretation: Transecting repair can be associated with penile complications.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The distinction from short bulbar strictures not related to straddle injury affects procedure selection.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Men with short bulbar strictures not related to straddle injury
decision_rules: Prefer non-transecting EPA or free graft urethroplasty over tEPA to limit erectile or penile complications.

recommended_regimens.name: ntEPA
recommended_regimens.summary: Use non-transecting excision and anastomosis instead of tEPA when suitable.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: Reported patency rates were 93.2-99% at median follow-ups ranging between 17.6 and 37.1 months.

recommended_regimens.name: FGU
recommended_regimens.summary: Use free graft reconstruction instead of tEPA for this non-straddle-injury short bulbar stricture.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: A cited RCT found patency of 88% with tEPA versus 87% with BMG FGU, without a significant difference.

response_assessment.method: Assess stricture recurrence, erectile function and penile complications
response_assessment.interpretation: The evidence summary reports similar patency across tEPA, ntEPA and FGU for this population, with fewer erectile or penile complications after ntEPA and FGU.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The evidence notation 1b-3* denotes LE1b for tEPA versus FGU and LE3 for the comparison involving tEPA, ntEPA and FGU. A planned ntEPA cannot always be completed.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Men with a bulbar stricture not amenable to excision and primary anastomosis
decision_rules: Use free graft urethroplasty if tension-free EPA is not feasible.
Select dorsal, dorsal-lateral or ventral graft placement according to expertise, practice and operative findings.

recommended_regimens.name: FGU
recommended_regimens.summary: Reconstruct a bulbar stricture unsuitable for EPA with a free graft.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: Reported bulbar FGU patency was 88-91% with twelve to 40 months follow-up.

response_assessment.method: Assess patency over time
response_assessment.interpretation: The guideline notes that patency may decline with longer follow-up.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The graft-location recommendation is Strong; its associated evidence level is 1b, and the guideline reports no patency advantage from a particular graft location. Buccal mucosa is the most widely used graft.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Men with a bulbar stricture unsuitable for EPA that contains a short, nearly obliterative portion
decision_rules: Consider an augmented anastomotic repair when only a short part of the longer strictured segment is nearly obliterative.

recommended_regimens.name: augmented anastomotic repair
recommended_regimens.summary: Excise the most obliterative portion, anastomose the urethral plate and augment the remaining reconstruction with an onlay graft.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: The evidence summary reports 88-92% patency for bulbar strictures with a nearly obliterative segment, with deterioration over time.

alternative_regimens.name: FGU
alternative_regimens.summary: Free graft reconstruction is the recommended broader approach when EPA is not feasible.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: Consider according to anatomy and the suitability of augmented anastomotic repair.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: A cited comparative study found higher recurrence risk with augmented anastomotic repair than with dorsal free graft urethroplasty.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Men fit for reconstruction with complex anterior disease involving the bulbar urethra and unsuitable for single-stage repair
decision_rules: Offer a staged approach when local conditions or previous procedures prevent suitable single-stage repair.
If LS is present, do not choose staged bulbar urethroplasty when a single-stage operation is possible.
Discuss staging with patients uncertain whether to choose perineal urethrostomy or urethral reconstruction.

recommended_regimens.name: staged urethroplasty
recommended_regimens.summary: Offer to fit patients with complex anterior disease unsuitable for a single-stage operation.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: The evidence summary reports 33.3-90% patency for staged repair of bulbar or bulbar-involving strictures, varying with patient and stricture characteristics.
recommended_regimens.duration_cycles: May require more than two stages.

alternative_regimens.name: perineal urethrostomy
alternative_regimens.summary: Another option to discuss when the patient is undecided about staged reconstruction.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: Patient preference and suitability for reconstruction.

not_recommended.name: staged bulbar urethroplasty for lichen sclerosis when single-stage urethroplasty is possible
not_recommended.reason: The guideline advises against staging in this circumstance; recommendation grade Weak.

response_assessment.method: Assess graft or stoma, need for revision and the patient's wish to proceed
response_assessment.interpretation: Up to 19% required revision of the first stage; up to 45.5% chose not to undergo second-stage re-tubularisation.

supportive_care: Warn patients that reconstruction may take more than two stages; recommendation grade Weak.
treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Potential indications include fistula, false passage, abscess, cancer, previous complex repair failure, radiotherapy-associated disease or severe spongiofibrosis. The role of staging for LS is disputed.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients requiring ReDo urethroplasty for a long recurrent stricture after a previous urethroplasty
decision_rules: Use an oral mucosa free graft for repeat reconstruction of a long stricture.

recommended_regimens.name: oral mucosa free graft urethroplasty
recommended_regimens.summary: Perform free graft ReDo urethroplasty for a long recurrent stricture.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: Rosenbaum et al. and Javali et al. reported patency rates of 82-86% with BMG FGU for ReDo cases.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The guideline's evidence summary states that buccal mucosa free graft repair after failed urethroplasty can attain patency comparable to primary repair.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients with extensive penobulbar or panurethral disease requiring complex reconstruction
decision_rules: Offer panurethral reconstruction in a specialised centre.
Combine techniques when one technique cannot cover the full stricture length.

recommended_regimens.name: panurethral urethroplasty
recommended_regimens.summary: Provide reconstruction in a specialised centre equipped to use different techniques and materials.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: A multi-institutional review by Warner et al. reported 77.5% overall patency among 466 patients with strictures > 8 cm.

recommended_regimens.name: combined reconstructive techniques
recommended_regimens.summary: Combine techniques if no single approach treats the entire panurethral stricture.

alternative_regimens.name: PU
alternative_regimens.summary: An alternative to complex reconstruction.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: The patient is unfit for complex reconstruction or declines it.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Published panurethral outcomes generally originate from high-volume centres; patency tends to be lower than after shorter reconstructions.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Men with complex anterior strictures, including those unfit for or unwilling to undergo formal reconstruction
decision_rules: Offer PU as a management option.
Select its type using patient characteristics and operator experience; consider augmented Gil-Vernet-Blandy or “7-flap” PU for proximal bulbar or membranous extension.

recommended_regimens.name: PU
recommended_regimens.summary: Offer perineal urethrostomy for complex anterior stricture disease.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: Retrospective series report patency rates of 70-95% at mean/median follow-up of 20–63 months.

alternative_regimens.name: augmented Gil-Vernet-Blandy perineal urethrostomy
alternative_regimens.summary: A PU configuration for disease reaching the proximal bulbar or membranous urethra.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: Proximal bulbar or membranous extension; recommendation grade Weak.

alternative_regimens.name: “7-flap” PU
alternative_regimens.summary: A PU configuration considered for proximal bulbar or membranous disease and for obese men.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: Relevant anatomy or obesity; recommendation grade Weak.

response_assessment.method: Assess stomal patency, complications, voiding and patient-reported outcomes
response_assessment.interpretation: Reported complications include wound problems, infection and post-micturition dribble; patency can decrease over time.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Offering PU specifically to patients unfit or unwilling to undergo reconstruction carries a Weak recommendation. The choice of PU configuration also carries a Weak recommendation.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients with non-obliterative VUAS or radiation-induced BMS
decision_rules: Start with visually controlled dilatation or DVIU.
During DVIU, avoid deep cuts at the six and twelve o’clock positions because of rectal injury and urosymphyseal fistulation risks.
Do not apply endoluminal treatment to completely obliterated VUAS, BMS or BNS.

recommended_regimens.name: visually controlled dilatation
recommended_regimens.summary: An initial endoluminal treatment for non-obliterative VUAS or radiation-induced BMS.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: The evidence summary reports 0-89% patency with visually controlled dilatation in the relevant non-obliterative posterior-stenosis series.

recommended_regimens.name: DVIU
recommended_regimens.summary: An initial endoluminal treatment for the same non-obliterative posterior lesions.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: The evidence summary reports 25-100% patency with DVIU in the relevant series.

not_recommended.name: deep DVIU incisions at six and twelve o’clock
not_recommended.reason: Deep cuts at these positions can injure the rectum or cause urosymphyseal fistulation, respectively; recommendation grade Strong.

not_recommended.name: endoluminal treatment of completely obliterated VUAS, BMS or BNS
not_recommended.reason: These lesions are unlikely to respond; recommendation grade Strong.

not_recommended.name: posterior urethral stents
not_recommended.reason: Low reported patency and substantial urinary-incontinence risk; recommendation grade Weak.

response_assessment.method: Assess patency and urinary continence
response_assessment.interpretation: The evidence summary warns of de novo UI in up to 25% and worsening of existing UI in up to 15% after endoluminal treatment.

supportive_care: Warn patients of new or worsening urinary incontinence after endoluminal treatment; recommendation grade Weak.
treatment_pathways.special_considerations: These interventions can be performed under loco-regional anaesthesia.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients with non-obliterative BNS after surgery for benign prostatic obstruction
decision_rules: Use TUR or “hot-knife” DVIU initially.
Avoid endoluminal treatment if the bladder neck is completely obliterated.

recommended_regimens.name: TUR
recommended_regimens.summary: An initial endoluminal option for non-obliterative BNS after BPO surgery.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: The evidence summary reports 58.3% patency for TUR in BNS.

recommended_regimens.name: “hot-knife” DVIU
recommended_regimens.summary: An initial incision option for this non-obliterative BNS setting.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: The evidence summary reports 72% patency for “hot-knife” incision in BNS.

not_recommended.name: endoluminal treatment in complete obliteration
not_recommended.reason: Complete obliteration is unlikely to respond; recommendation grade Strong.

response_assessment.method: Assess patency and urinary continence
response_assessment.interpretation: New or aggravated urinary incontinence can follow endoluminal intervention.

supportive_care: Warn patients about possible new or worsened urinary incontinence; recommendation grade Weak.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients with recurrent non-obliterative VUAS or BNS after endoluminal treatment
decision_rules: Repeat endoluminal treatment may be used to stabilise non-obliterative VUAS or BNS.
For recurrent posterior stenosis, ISD is a possible stabilising measure, especially when surgery is unsuitable or unwanted.
Restrict MMC injection to a clinical trial.

recommended_regimens.name: repeat endoluminal treatments
recommended_regimens.summary: Repeat treatment in an attempt to stabilise non-obliterative VUAS or BNS.

alternative_regimens.name: ISD
alternative_regimens.summary: May stabilise recurrent posterior stenosis after dilatation or DVIU.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: Particularly relevant for patients unfit for or unwilling to have surgery, or for radiation-induced BMS.

not_recommended.name: MMC outside a clinical trial
not_recommended.reason: Rare but severe reported complications included osteitis pubis, bladder neck necrosis and rectourethral fistula.

not_recommended.name: posterior urethral stents
not_recommended.reason: Reported patency was 47-60% with urinary incontinence of 19-82%; recommendation grade Weak.

response_assessment.method: Cystoscopy to exclude stenosis recurrence
response_assessment.interpretation: The guide advises waiting three to four months after DVIU before proceeding to incontinence surgery when needed; other cited practice waits for twelve months.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: ISD can reduce quality of life and adherence may be poor. The cited intralesional-injection series were retrospective and lacked trials comparing treatment with and without injections.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Non-irradiated patients, or irradiated patients with adequate bladder function, with obliterative VUAS or VUAS refractory to endoluminal treatment
decision_rules: Consider ReDo VUA when the patient is fit and bladder function is adequate.
Take continence, stenosis anatomy and previous radiotherapy into account; offer a retropubic approach if continence is present before surgery.
Avoid reconstruction when urethral necrosis, calcification, fistulation or inadequate bladder function makes it unsuitable.

recommended_regimens.name: ReDo VUA
recommended_regimens.summary: Reconstruct obliterative or endoluminal-treatment-refractory VUAS in appropriately selected patients.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: The evidence summary reports patency of 60-91% in non-irradiated patients and 67% in irradiated patients.

alternative_regimens.name: retropubic ReDo VUA
alternative_regimens.summary: An approach offered when the patient is continent before surgery.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: Pre-operative urinary continence; recommendation grade Weak.

response_assessment.timepoint: At least three to six months after ReDo VUA
response_assessment.method: Confirm stable VUA patency before considering AUS
response_assessment.interpretation: After a transperineal approach, urinary incontinence is expected and later anti-incontinence surgery may be required.

supportive_care: Warn that transperineal ReDo VUA inevitably results in UI and that a subsequent anti-UI operation may be needed after at least three to six months; recommendation grade Strong.
treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The panel advises reconstruction in experienced high-volume centres, particularly after radiotherapy or other ablative treatments. The retropubic and transperineal approaches have not been directly compared for incontinence.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients with BNS refractory to endoscopic treatment after surgery for benign prostatic obstruction
decision_rules: Reconstruct the bladder neck with local advancement when endoscopic treatment has failed.

recommended_regimens.name: Y-V or T-plasty
recommended_regimens.summary: Augment the bladder neck with local bladder flaps for treatment-refractory BNS.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: The evidence summary reports 83-100% patency and de novo incontinence of up to 14% after bladder neck reconstruction.

response_assessment.method: Assess bladder neck patency and new urinary incontinence

supportive_care: Warn patients about possible de novo urinary incontinence; recommendation grade Strong.
treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The local flap may be advanced with or without scar resection.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients with BMS after TURP or simple prostatectomy who require reconstruction
decision_rules: Manage according to bulbar-stricture principles, choosing anastomotic or graft augmentation repair by stricture length and tightness.

recommended_regimens.name: EPA
recommended_regimens.summary: A reconstructive option selected according to the length and tightness of BMS after BPO surgery.

recommended_regimens.name: augmentation urethroplasty with a graft
recommended_regimens.summary: A reconstructive option when the stricture's length or tightness calls for augmentation.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: Kulkarni et al. reported patency of 81.8% with dorsal versus 84.6% with ventral onlay urethroplasty after mean follow-up of 14 months.

response_assessment.method: Assess patency and continence
response_assessment.interpretation: The evidence summary reports incontinence in up to 25% after BMS reconstruction following BPO surgery.

supportive_care: Warn about de novo urinary incontinence after reconstruction; recommendation grade Strong.
treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Reconstruction is close to the external sphincter, and prior BPO surgery may already have damaged the bladder neck.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients with short (< 2.5 cm) radiation-induced BMS refractory to endoscopic treatment
decision_rules: Choose EPA or augmentation urethroplasty according to surgeon experience and stricture characteristics.
Counsel about new urinary incontinence and erectile dysfunction.

recommended_regimens.name: EPA
recommended_regimens.summary: One surgical option for a short radiation-induced BMS after endoscopic treatment failure.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: A systematic review reported pooled patency of 80% for urethroplasty, without a significant difference between EPA and augmentation.

recommended_regimens.name: augmentation urethroplasty
recommended_regimens.summary: Another surgical option for this short radiation-induced BMS setting.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: The same systematic review reported pooled patency of 80% across EPA and augmentation, without a significant between-technique difference.

response_assessment.method: Assess patency, new incontinence and erectile function
response_assessment.interpretation: The evidence summary reports de novo incontinence in 19-26% and new ED in 0-35% after surgery for radiation-induced BMS.

supportive_care: Warn about new incontinence and erectile dysfunction; recommendation grade Strong.
treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Radiation-related tissue injury can impair healing beyond the visible stenosis.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients with long (> 2.5 cm) radiation-induced BMS
decision_rules: Use augmentation urethroplasty for a long radiation-induced BMS; a long bulbar component generally prevents EPA.

recommended_regimens.name: augmentation urethroplasty
recommended_regimens.summary: Reconstruct radiation-induced BMS > 2.5 cm by augmentation.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: The evidence summary reports pooled urethroplasty patency of 80% for radiation-induced BMS, without a significant difference between EPA and augmentation in the systematic review.

response_assessment.method: Assess patency, de novo urinary incontinence and new erectile dysfunction
response_assessment.interpretation: The evidence summary reports de novo incontinence in 19-26% and new ED in 0-35% after radiation-induced BMS surgery.

supportive_care: Warn about de novo incontinence and new erectile dysfunction; recommendation grade Strong.
treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Radiation-induced BMS longer than 2-2.5 cm are rarely suitable for EPA.

treatment_pathways.condition: prostatic strictures secondary to radiation/high energy sources
treatment_pathways.patient_population: Motivated, fit patients with adequate bladder function and a prostatic stricture after irradiation or high-energy treatment
decision_rules: Offer salvage prostatectomy when appropriate after considering the morbidity of this operation.
If bladder function is impaired or urethral necrosis or peri-urethral disease is present, consider diversion instead.

recommended_regimens.name: salvage prostatectomy
recommended_regimens.summary: Offer to a fit, motivated patient with sufficient bladder function and treatment-related prostatic stricture.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: Mundy et al. reported patency in six of nine patients (67%); one (11%) required AUS for severe incontinence.

alternative_regimens.name: supravesical diversion
alternative_regimens.summary: Consider when preservation of the urethral outlet is unsuitable.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: Impaired bladder function, urethral necrosis or peri-urethral pathology, particularly if pain or spasms prevent tolerance of a suprapubic catheter.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The reported salvage-prostatectomy morbidity includes rectal injury, VUAS and incontinence. The reported “pull-through” reconstruction requires further validation before it can be recommended.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients with recurrent or complex disease, loss of bladder capacity and/or incapacitating local symptoms
decision_rules: Perform urinary diversion when lower urinary tract reconstruction is unsuitable or symptoms are incapacitating.
Add cystectomy during diversion for intractable bladder pain, spasms and/or haematuria.

recommended_regimens.name: urinary diversion
recommended_regimens.summary: Divert urine in recurrent or complex cases with reduced bladder capacity or disabling local symptoms.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: The evidence summary reports improved QoL and high satisfaction in patients with a devastated lower urinary tract.

recommended_regimens.name: cystectomy during urinary diversion
recommended_regimens.summary: Include cystectomy when pain, spasms or haematuria are intractable.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: The evidence summary states that cystectomy can palliate intractable bladder pain, spasms and haematuria.

response_assessment.method: Assess relief of local symptoms and quality of life

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Choice of diversion depends on bladder capacity, symptoms, performance status and patient expectations.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients with a short (< 1.5 cm), non-obliterative posterior stenosis after trauma
decision_rules: One endoluminal attempt can be made for a short, non-obliterative lesion.
Do not perform endoscopic treatment for obliterative stenosis.

recommended_regimens.name: endoluminal treatment
recommended_regimens.summary: Make one attempt using endoscopic incision or dilatation for a short, non-obliterative traumatic posterior stenosis.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: Reported outcomes vary substantially between cited series; a review combining obliterative and non-obliterative lesions calculated a 20% composite stricture-free rate.

not_recommended.name: endoscopic treatment for obliterative stenosis
not_recommended.reason: It is not successful and may create a false passage towards the bladder or rectum; recommendation grade Strong.

response_assessment.method: Assess persistent stenosis and need for definitive reconstruction
response_assessment.interpretation: Repeated curative-intent endoluminal procedures are discouraged because they can delay definitive repair.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Deferred management of PFUI is undertaken at earliest three months after trauma.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients with a short (< 1 cm), non-obliterative recurrence after excision and primary anastomosis
decision_rules: Endoluminal treatment may be used for a short non-obliterative post-EPA recurrence.
If durable patency is the goal, do not perform more than two DVIUs and/or dilatations.

alternative_regimens.name: DVIU and/or dilatation
alternative_regimens.summary: Treat a short, non-obliterative post-EPA recurrence endoluminally, within the stated limit on repeated attempts.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: Recurrence < 1 cm without complete obliteration; the limit of no more than two procedures for long-term patency has a Weak recommendation.

not_recommended.name: more than two DVIUs and/or dilatations for durable patency
not_recommended.reason: Three or more incisions have not been successful in the cited recurrence series; the recommendation against additional curative-intent attempts is Weak.

response_assessment.method: Assess stricture-free status
response_assessment.interpretation: The evidence summary reports 22.9-77.3% stricture-free rates after a first DVIU for a short, non-obliterative post-EPA recurrence.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Further repetitive endoluminal treatment is considered palliative rather than a route to durable cure.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients with obliterative traumatic posterior stenosis
decision_rules: Perform progressive perineal EPA in a high-volume centre.
Use a midline perineal incision; reserve abdomino-perineal reconstruction for particularly complicated anatomy.

recommended_regimens.name: progressive perineal EPA
recommended_regimens.summary: Provide definitive open reconstruction for obliterative post-traumatic posterior stenosis.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: The guideline reports 85.7% overall patency after deferred EPA.
recommended_regimens.duration_cycles: Deferred management occurs at earliest three months after trauma.

alternative_regimens.name: abdomino-perineal reconstruction
alternative_regimens.summary: Reserve a combined approach for a very long distraction defect, para-urethral bladder base fistula, trauma-related recto-urethral fistula or bladder neck injury.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: The specified complicated circumstances; recommendation grade Weak.

not_recommended.name: endoscopic treatment
not_recommended.reason: Obliterative stenosis does not respond and false passages may occur; recommendation grade Strong.

not_recommended.name: total pubectomy during abdomino-perineal reconstruction
not_recommended.reason: It has higher complication rates than partial pubectomy without improving surgical exposure; recommendation grade Strong.

response_assessment.method: Assess patency, continence, sexual function and rectal injury
response_assessment.interpretation: The guideline reports incontinence of 6.8-8.5% and rectal injury of 0-10.2% after deferred EPA.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Open reconstruction in this setting is recommended only in high-volume centres, with a Weak strength rating. The midline-incision recommendation is Strong.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients with non-obliterative posterior traumatic stenosis after failed initial endoluminal treatment
decision_rules: Proceed to progressive perineal EPA after failure of the initial endoluminal approach.

recommended_regimens.name: progressive perineal EPA
recommended_regimens.summary: Provide open reconstruction for non-obliterative traumatic posterior stenosis after endoluminal failure.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: The guideline reports 85.7% overall patency after deferred EPA for post-traumatic posterior stenosis.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: A midline perineal incision is strongly recommended; reconstruction should be undertaken in a high-volume centre.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Motivated patients with recurrence after a first urethroplasty who do not wish to accept palliative endoluminal treatment or urinary diversion
decision_rules: Offer repeat urethroplasty after failure of the first repair.
Consider another EPA when tension-free anastomosis remains possible; select other reconstructive tissue when it is not.
Use a local flap to fill excessive dead space or separate repairs when a concomitant recto-urethral fistula is corrected.

recommended_regimens.name: ReDo-urethroplasty
recommended_regimens.summary: Offer another open repair to appropriately motivated patients after the first failed urethroplasty.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: Across the reported types of repeat urethroplasty, patency varied between 50-100%.

alternative_regimens.name: Badenoch pull-through technique
alternative_regimens.summary: A reconstructive option when satisfactory mucosa-to-mucosa suturing cannot be achieved.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: Deep proximal urethral location or inability to achieve adequate anastomotic suturing.

alternative_regimens.name: tubed preputial island flap
alternative_regimens.summary: An alternative reconstruction if tension-free anastomosis cannot be achieved or bulbar tissue is ischaemic or necrotic.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: Anastomosis remains under tension despite length-gaining measures, or bulbar urethral ischaemia/necrosis.

alternative_regimens.name: staged BMG urethroplasty with flap
alternative_regimens.summary: An alternative reconstruction for an unsuitable anastomosis or compromised bulbar tissue.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: Tension-free anastomosis is impossible or bulbar tissue is ischaemic or necrotic.

alternative_regimens.name: staged buccal mucosa dartos flap
alternative_regimens.summary: An alternative staged reconstructive option.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: Tension-free anastomosis is impossible or bulbar tissue is ischaemic or necrotic.

alternative_regimens.name: radial forearm free flap urethroplasty
alternative_regimens.summary: An alternative tissue-transfer reconstruction.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: Tension-free anastomosis is impossible or bulbar tissue is ischaemic or necrotic.

alternative_regimens.name: entero-urethroplasty
alternative_regimens.summary: An alternative reconstruction requiring a competent bladder neck.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: Tension-free anastomosis is impossible or bulbar tissue is ischaemic or necrotic, and the bladder neck is competent.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Local tissue flaps for excessive dead space or concomitant recto-urethral fistula have a Weak recommendation. If reconstructive treatment is declined or unsuitable, described alternatives include Mitrofanoffvesicostomy, PU or permanent suprapubic diversion.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Women with an uncomplicated FUS
decision_rules: Begin with urethral dilatation because it is minimally invasive and has a low reported complication rate.

recommended_regimens.name: urethral dilatation
recommended_regimens.summary: Dilate the urethra as initial treatment of FUS.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: The evidence summary reports mean stricture-free rate of 40.1% after dilatation alone at mean follow-up 36 (12-59) months.

response_assessment.method: Assess patency, urinary symptoms and recurrence
response_assessment.interpretation: Repeat dilatation by itself is unlikely to cure a recurrent stricture.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Reported new-onset SUI after dilatation was 1.4%.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Women with a first recurrence of FUS
decision_rules: Repeat dilatation and institute planned weekly ISD, or arrange planned repeat dilatation.
Present continuing dilatation as palliation rather than definitive cure.

recommended_regimens.name: repeat urethral dilatation and ISD
recommended_regimens.summary: Repeat dilatation after a first recurrence and begin scheduled weekly self-dilatation.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: The evidence summary reports 97% patency with dilatation followed by ISD or planned repeat dilatation as palliation at mean FU 6-21 months; continuing instrumentation does not establish stricture-free status.
recommended_regimens.duration_cycles: Weekly ISD with a 16-18 Fr catheter

alternative_regimens.name: planned repeat dilatation
alternative_regimens.summary: A planned palliation approach instead of weekly ISD.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: First recurrence of FUS when repeat planned dilatation is selected.

response_assessment.method: Assess symptoms, patency and need for further intervention
response_assessment.interpretation: A patent lumen maintained through ongoing ISD or dilatation is not equivalent to being stricture-free.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The evidence summary reports 26.6% patency after isolated repeat dilatation.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Women with a second recurrence of FUS who cannot perform ISD or want definitive treatment
decision_rules: Perform urethroplasty.
Select the technique based on surgeon experience, availability and quality of graft or flap tissue, and the condition of the ventral versus dorsal urethra.

recommended_regimens.name: urethroplasty
recommended_regimens.summary: Offer definitive reconstruction after a second recurrence under the specified patient conditions.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: The evidence summary reports urethroplasty patency of 62.5-100%; VOBMG and DOBMG reported ranges were 92-100% and 62.5-100%, respectively.

response_assessment.method: Assess recurrent narrowing, voiding function and new urinary incontinence
response_assessment.interpretation: Reported outcomes vary among graft and flap techniques.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Described reconstructive materials include vaginal grafts or flaps, labial/vestibular grafts or flaps, BMG and LMG. The recommendation does not designate a universally preferred graft or flap.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Female patients with a short meatal stricture
decision_rules: Treat a short meatal lesion with meatotomy/meatoplasty.

recommended_regimens.name: meatotomy/meatoplasty
recommended_regimens.summary: Use meatal surgery for a short female meatal stricture.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: The evidence summary reports a 97% success rate at twelve months follow-up; the described series of 50 girls reported patency in 96%.

response_assessment.method: Assess patency, recurrent UTI and voiding symptoms
response_assessment.interpretation: In the cited series, 48 of 50 patients had resolution of recurrent UTIs and improved voiding symptoms one year after meatoplasty.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Trans men within six months after neophalloplasty with severe obstructive symptoms affecting quality of life, recurrent UTI or urinary retention
decision_rules: Avoid endoscopic incision and urethroplasty within six months of neophalloplasty while local tissues heal.
Use suprapubic drainage first for severe early obstruction; specialist perineostomy is another option.

recommended_regimens.name: suprapubic catheter
recommended_regimens.summary: The stated first-line drainage option for severe early obstruction, recurrent UTI or retention after neophallic reconstruction.

alternative_regimens.name: perineostomy
alternative_regimens.summary: An alternative early outlet procedure that can be closed during later formal reconstruction.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: Performed by a urologist familiar with transgender urethral anatomy.
